look_here_first: Look closely at foliage and calyx: low dense clumps with narrow cauline leaves and conspicuous tack-shaped glandular hairs; the calyx is strongly ribbed with tiny awned tips.
project_tracker_diagnostic: Low dense perennial with only cauline narrow leaves, tack-shaped glandular hairs, repeated 3-flowered cymes, strongly 10-ridged awned calyces, and a pale strongly marked lower corolla lip.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays native list, Travis preserve records, UT Williamson County treatment, and Comal County herbarium material; no county presence inferred.

morphology_keys.habit: Perennial low dense clump with many stems.
morphology_keys.leaves: Only cauline narrow leaves; paired bases can form a short sheath across the node.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: 3-flowered cymes repeated at closely spaced nodes.
morphology_keys.calyx: Strongly 10-ridged with short awned lobe tips.
morphology_keys.floral_detail: Pale blue-violet corolla with a broad white/violet-marked lower lip.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Texas sage has basal leaves and pitted/sunken glands. Azure sage is much taller and more open.
